Senses.Note: Allowlist count: 168 hits in 73 texts. Variants include emphatic take care not to get it wrong (莫錯會好) and just do not get it wrong (且莫錯會). One imperative sense; preceding statements do not create different referents.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Anguo Hongtao section. Anguo Hongtao is the exact respondent who answers a monk's question about the meaning of coming from the West with, 'It is so, but do not understand it wrongly.'

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): (五燈全書)(第34卷-第120卷). Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書), Songru Daomi section. Songru Daomi is the exact hall speaker who tells the assembly to look carefully and not understand yesterday's snow and today's thaw wrongly.

Occurrences.Kwic: 莫是真實相為麼。莫是正恁麼時無一法可證麼。莫是認伊來處麼。莫是全體顯露麼。莫錯會好。如此見解。喚作依草附木。與佛法天地懸隔。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Correct Lineage of Chan (禪宗正脉), Tiantai Deshao section. After asking how the assembly construes his answers, Tiantai Deshao himself lists four proposed construals, warns 'do not understand wrongly,' and calls those views dependence on grass and attachment to trees.

SearchAliases: Zen do not get it wrong
Senses.Explanation: An imperative: do not (莫) understand or take it (會) wrongly (錯). Its distinct Chan deployment is as warnings that named speakers attach directly to a saying or answer in public discourse. Asked the intention of the coming from the West, Anguo Hongtao answers 'it is so, but do not get it wrong.' An extended address says not to infer 'not round and not sudden' from the preceding words and not to present borrowed, similar, or calculated phrases as one's own understanding, repeating 'do not get it wrong.' Elsewhere Bao’en Huiming warns an assembly not to say that speech, silence, movement, and stillness are all buddha-affairs. The formula can also follow an unexplained seasonal statement — 'yesterday snow, today it melts' — leaving the warning itself as the only explicit appraisal. These contexts establish the public-interview function without supplying an interpretation of what the preceding words secretly mean.
